V1_saved_resume_point_identity.note: the resume point launch2 saved is the same state launch1 had after its batch 0, so the two runs are comparable from episode 4 onward

V2_resumed_rollouts_match_the_uninterrup.evidence_level: A (direct byte comparison) on the two episodes the resume actually reached before the construction quota was spent

V3_resumed_rollouts_carried_the_restored.note: the rollout rows record the lambda they were sampled with, so this shows the restored state really fed the continued rollouts rather than only being stored in a file

V4_stop_reason.harness_defect_registered: r35_launch.py bound the per-directory cap to the round's remaining budget without adding the starts this directory had already recorded, so launch2 was effectively capped at 6 fresh episodes; the direction of the error is conservative (it stopped early, it never overran the quota)
V4_stop_reason.refused_start: train_s11_e6 (scenario 1300005) was refused by the real ledger with 'launch cap 7 reached at 7' because launch2's own book already carried the crashed attempt

covered_indirectly: post-resume update correctness: R4 recomputes batch 0's update from the restored ep0 milestone and reproduces the recorded post-update parameter hash, lambda and step count byte for byte

collector non-interference: V2's byte-identical resumed cells plus the A-grade episode 0..3 comparison in PASSIVITY_EVIDENCE.json plus the pure wiring probe in LAUNCH2_ATTEMPT1_REPRO.json (rng, clock, registry and publish counters)
not_executed: the update that would have followed the resumed rollouts in launch2: the quota stopped the rollouts at six episodes, so launch2 never reached its own second batch update
the live collector probe during launch2: the probe's records lived in the process memory and the run ended on the ledger refusal before the dump
a third runner invocation: not authorised, and the one the user approved is spent
V5_uncovered_after_the_resume.residual_risk_for_frozen_training: the corrected timing changes which action row owns each credit, so a 128-episode run's trajectory will not match the archived legacy run; that is the point of the fix, not a defect, but it means old trajectories cannot be reused as predictions
